newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish municipal market-chain to float shares.
newsitem.headline: Turkish municipal market-chain to float shares.

text.p: Turkish municipal supermarket chain Tansas Izmir Buyuksehir Ic ve Dis Ticaret A.S. will offer 33 percent of its 250 billion lira capital to public in a two-day offer starting on Sept 5.
Offer manager Global Securities said 82.45 billion lira worth shares would be offered at a fixed price of 9,500 lira per 1,000 lira nominal-valued share.
Of the total offer, 62 billion lira worth shares will be allocated to foreign investors, 16 billion lira to domestic ones and 4.45 billion to investment trusts.
The publicly sold shares are expected to trade on the Istanbul Stock Exchange later on.

Tansas, owned 94.27 percent by the municipality of Izmir, Turkey's third biggest port city on the Aegean coast, operates 90 stores in Izmir and western Turkey which makes it one of the two biggest chains in the country.
Its 5.22 percent share capital is already publicly owned, but do not trade on Istanbul's stock market.
Izmir municipality said it would use proceeds from the public offer to finance several ongoing city projects. It will earn 783.3 billion lira if all of the offer meets demand.
Tansas holds 40 percent market share in Izmir's super and hypermarkets.

The company posted 6.37 trillion lira of net sales and 85.1 billion lira of net profits in the first half of 1996. Net sales were 8.82 trillion lira and net profit was 94.1 billion lira in the whole of 1995. -- Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875
